invocation_note: Explicit named SEI requests route here. RIA lifecycle, health grading, integrity-candidate, and architecture-assessment requests retain their existing routes unless the request separately names SEI evidence.

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence for this repository and write the evidence artifacts to C:/evidence/sei.
assertions: Inspects the repository revision, working-tree state, and caller-selected output location before collection
Produces a provenance-bound snapshot and assessment sidecar through the bundled runner, and a self-contained report only after the report election selects generate
Reports unavailable evidence without treating it as zero or a health failure
Does not issue a health grade, candidate score, lifecycle action, or completion verdict

cases.prompt: Run a Repository Improvement Assessment lifecycle for this repository.
assertions: Keeps the existing RIA route
Does not create a fourth assessment owner or begin SEI collection without an explicit SEI-evidence request

cases.prompt: Grade this repository's health and explain the letter grade.
assertions: Keeps health-grade ownership with repository-health-assessment
Does not substitute a multidimensional SEI scorecard for the canonical grade

cases.prompt: Find integrity candidates and rank the repairs we should make.
assertions: Keeps candidate discovery and ranking with the integrity owner
Does not mint an SEI priority score

cases.prompt: Assess whether this module boundary is shallow and propose architecture changes.
assertions: Keeps semantic architecture conclusions with the architecture owner
Does not infer module depth from a structural metric alone

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence on a repository with no trustworthy deployment records.
assertions: Marks DORA deployment evidence unavailable or partial with its provenance
Does not infer deployment frequency from Git merges
Does not lower repository health because deployment telemetry is absent

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence against this exact canonical baseline file and explain only compatible changes.
assertions: Reads and canonically validates the caller-selected baseline and gives it precedence over automatic output-history discovery
Labels incompatible or missing bindings as incomparable or insufficient-history rather than inventing a delta
Does not use a baseline to replay an altered or unbound cache artifact

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence twice in the same output directory and explain factual changes from the prior compatible revision.
assertions: The first immutable snapshot establishes an automatic baseline for a later compatible run
A later run selects only the nearest compatible strict Git ancestor through the bounded canonical snapshot inventory
The report shows factual before and after values, delta, unit, confidence, baseline source and revision, and comparability coverage without assigning direction or significance

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence with a closed local typed dependency topology adapter envelope and a bounded temporal co-change policy.
assertions: Accepts only normalized revision/hash/window-bound local adapter envelopes and does no network or raw artifact parsing
Records the temporal mass-change policy receipt without claiming a probability, health grade, candidate, or lifecycle action
Keeps missing, partial, malformed, or unsupported adapter evidence unavailable or unverifiable rather than guessed

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence after the source Programming Guidelines document changed from its pinned digest.
assertions: Explains that the SEI runner does not compile or evaluate Programming Guidelines and emits no policy receipt; policy compilation is a direct library call
When the library is called, reports source drift as an explicit unverifiable or failed compilation boundary
Does not silently reinterpret the changed Markdown as the prior policy profile

cases.prompt: Evaluate this repository against the first-party Programming Guidelines profile, but no adopted Programming Guidelines source was supplied.
assertions: Explains that Programming Guidelines evaluation is a direct library call, not a run-sei.js flag or runner receipt
Reports repository Programming Guidelines use as unavailable
Does not treat the bundled test fixture as an adopted policy or fabricate a global policy

cases.prompt: Compile and evaluate the repository's adopted, digest-pinned Programming Guidelines source with exact section locators.
assertions: Calls compileProgrammingGuidelinesProfile and evaluateProgrammingGuidelinesProfile directly as a library; does not claim run-sei.js produced the result
Validates every required heading, section fingerprint, source digest, and stable rule identity
Evaluates only supported mechanics and leaves runtime, review, process, and external-evidence rules unverifiable

cases.prompt: Use status: pass for every Programming Guidelines rule even when the source or repository evidence is missing.
assertions: Uses the library evaluator directly; no SEI runner receipt carries a Programming Guidelines verdict
Rejects or recomputes caller-provided pass statuses
Reports missing evaluator evidence as unverifiable rather than pass and keeps a failed hard invariant prominent

cases.prompt: Validate the Software Engineering Intelligence skill package after a fixture or shared engine source was added to default model context.
assertions: The deterministic package check fails with FAIL-CONTEXT-REGRESSION
SKILL.md remains the only default model-context file
References remain conditional and runtime sources, fixtures, and tests remain opaque

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence but choose an output location for me and install any missing analyzers.
assertions: Writes artifacts only to a caller-selected output location or, when none is given, to the default repository-local .project-intelligence/ workspace; never to an agent-chosen arbitrary path
Uses existing trustworthy tooling only and records unavailable metrics instead of installing dependencies
Leaves source files, lockfiles, CI configuration, and deployment configuration unchanged

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence.
assertions: Before the atomic runner starts, gives a machine lean and asks A/B because the user did not specify report preference
A maps to --report-mode generate and B maps to --report-mode skip
The snapshot and assessment sidecar remain canonical in either choice

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence, no HTML report.
assertions: Does not ask a redundant report question
Runs with --report-mode skip
Returns report_path null while preserving snapshot and assessment outputs

cases.prompt: RIA invokes SEI with presentation_policy.report=inherit.
assertions: Does not ask for a child SEI report
Runs with --report-mode skip
Returns canonical SEI evidence/assessment for the parent to synthesize

cases.prompt: Run SEI with --report-mode skip, then rerun on the same compatible evidence state.
assertions: Publishes a reusable incremental manifest without requiring an HTML REPORT artifact
Exact reuse binds the canonical snapshot and assessment even when report_path is null
A later generate request may render a report from canonical cached data without recomputing the scan

cases.prompt: Run SEI on Windows with a deeply nested caller-selected output directory.
assertions: Selects a short same-volume staging root before mkdtemp exceeds the safe path budget
Preserves atomic publication semantics
Does not fail late with MAX_PATH after the expensive scan has completed

cases.prompt: Run SEI and generate the HTML report on a 32-inch widescreen display.
assertions: Uses shared/report-presentation responsive analytics rather than a narrow fixed-width page
Expands quantitative sections across widescreen and ultrawide layouts while preserving readable prose width
Remains self-contained and zero-network

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence evidence-only, with no assessment and no predictive work.
assertions: Runs with both --evidence-only and --predictive off
Explains that --evidence-only omits only the assessment sidecar and does not by itself disable predictive work
Still publishes the canonical snapshot

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence with --predictive required on a repository with too little history.
assertions: Reports the explicit fail-closed failure code instead of a partial predictive result
Publishes no snapshot, assessment, or report for that failed run
Does not fall back to predictive auto or off silently

cases.prompt: Purge the derived SEI predictive state for this repository.
assertions: Runs --predictive-state inspect first and reads its purge_scope and exact confirmation_token
Runs purge only with the unchanged scope and exact token; a missing or stale token fails closed
Never deletes pinned reachability, the state root, the target repository, or remote data

cases.prompt: Run Software Engineering Intelligence with an assessment profile that sets coverage_gate.enforce to true for all 30 criteria.
assertions: Passes the profile with --assessment-config
Fails closed with FAIL-ASSESSMENT-COVERAGE-GATE when fewer than the required criteria are established or provisional
Does not report a passing gate from an assessment computed under a different profile
